lq.ANSWER:
Q1 — The dialogue within

  DEFINITE — single expected answer 

Model answer:  Self-exploration is a dialogue — first between the teacher and the student, then within one's own self. This inner dialogue is between what I am (my desire, thought, expectation, my competence) and what I really want to be (my natural acceptance, my intention). When the two are in harmony, the result is happiness; when in contradiction, unhappiness. The process has three parts: discover our natural acceptance (where we want to reach), find out what we are (where we are now), and ensure this dialogue and harmony within by evaluating our desires against our natural acceptance. As we refer to our natural acceptance, we become self-referential (self-organised, swatantra).

Q2 — Natural acceptance and its characteristics

  DEFINITE — single expected answer 

Model answer:  Natural acceptance is what I accept innately; we have the innate potential to recognise what is right because we are endowed with it. Its characteristics: it is innate (part and parcel of our being); invariant, uncorrupted by pre-conditioning; definite; and universal, the same for all human beings across time and place. It must be distinguished from liking or appeal, which varies from person to person and concerns the details of how a relationship is fulfilled. Natural acceptance has to do with my relationship to the reality of concern and my purpose or role at different levels of existence (e.g. natural acceptance for nurturing the body).

Q3 — Content and process of self-exploration

  DEFINITE — single expected answer 

Model answer:  The content of self-exploration is our basic human desire — happiness, prosperity and the continuity of both. We can verify that we desire happiness, prosperity and the continuity of both, and that if these are ensured there is nothing further we would desire; our desires are not unlimited. The process is self-investigation and self-verification: whatever is stated is a proposal, to be verified on our own right (not assuming it true or false) on the basis of natural acceptance, followed by experiential validation through living accordingly — leading to right understanding, and ultimately to living in harmony within, with others and with the entire existence.
